parsed.attack: The functional invite is real but terminates by construction: the thread is scoped to one parent, so the second sibling joins and then has nobody left to invite, the branching factor drops to zero at the household boundary, and every further household must be acquired cold. The invite is also asymmetric in the wrong direction - the inviter gets the record, the invitee is recruited into a recurring chore ('dictate thirty seconds after every call, every time') - which is exactly the friction the pain statement admits killed the incumbent care apps. The founder's own target is 40% second-sibling acceptance, which is k = 0.4 for one hop and zero thereafter: at the bottom of the healthy 0.3-0.7 band on the single turn the loop is capable of.
parsed.strongest_defence: Caregiving is a phase peers discuss constantly, and today's invited sibling is often the first user in their own family's crisis a year later; caregiver forums and r/AgingParents are free channels where the demo carries itself as a story - 'it told me what the furnace guy said in March and who paid him' - which is the whole product in one sentence.
parsed.verdict_reason: The invite converts one sibling and then dead-ends at the household boundary, so the loop is capped at a single hop and cannot compound.
